I am 67 years old, and this land has been my life for 40 years. I never went to school, but I know every corner of my 12 mu in Quzhou. My family has four mouths to feed, so I cannot take foolish risks. I will put 8 mu into my wheat-maize rotation, which has never let me down, and the remaining 4 mu into cotton for cash.

My winter wheat is already in the ground from last autumn. I sowed an improved variety — I have used Luyuan and Jimai types for years, and they do well here. I will topdress urea when the wheat greens up and again at jointing. I irrigate four times from the well: at green-up, jointing, heading, and grain filling. The wheat needs two pesticide sprays, mainly for aphids and rust. Before every wheat sowing I run the rotary tiller to prepare the seedbed. I expect about 450 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.

For summer maize, I plant Denghai 605 hybrid seed immediately after wheat harvest in June. I use the no-till planter straight into the wheat stubble — there is no time to waste between crops. I put down compound fertilizer at sowing and topdress urea when the plants flare. Two irrigations are usually enough in summer, and one spray keeps the corn borer away. I expect around 520 kg per mu.

For cotton on the 4 mu, I plough deep in spring and plant my improved cotton seed. Cotton is fussy — it needs three irrigations and four pesticide sprays for bollworm and aphids. I give it extra potassium because cotton fruits heavily. I expect about 100 kg of lint per mu.

I do what has worked. The university people in Quzhou have shown us new tricks over the years, and I have picked up what makes sense. My well water is reliable, and I watch the sky and the crops every day.
